title: Mascot: Predicting Memory Dependencies and Opportunities for Speculative Memory Bypassing
problem: Memory dependence prediction (MDP) and speculative memory bypassing (SMB) require conflicting predictor properties: MDP tolerates false positives but not false negatives, while SMB tolerates false negatives but not false positives. Prior TAGE-based predictors for either mechanism fail to learn patterns of non-dependence, causing inaccuracy.
motivation: Improving instruction-level parallelism (ILP) in out-of-order processors by enabling more aggressive load scheduling requires a unified predictor that can simultaneously satisfy the divergent accuracy requirements of MDP and SMB.
method: Mascot is a TAGE-inspired predictor that learns both dependence and non-dependence contexts. Unlike prior designs that only learn dependence patterns, Mascot tracks the history of non-aliasing outcomes in the TAGE table entries, enabling low false negative rates required for MDP and low false positive rates required for SMB from a single shared structure. The predictor is used in two modes: MDP-only (for load issue gating) and combined MDP+SMB (for value forwarding from store to load bypassing address resolution).
key_novelty: A unified TAGE-based predictor that explicitly learns non-dependence patterns, enabling both memory dependence prediction and speculative memory bypassing with a single compact hardware structure.
contributions: Mascot unified predictor that learns dependence and non-dependence contexts for both MDP and SMB
0.4% IPC gain over prior state-of-the-art MDP predictor at same size
1.9% average IPC gain (up to 26% peak) when enabling both MDP and SMB
Mascot-opt: compact 10.1 KiB variant achieving similar gains within 0.1% of full Mascot

metrics.speedup: 1.9% average IPC improvement (peak 26%) for MDP+SMB over baseline; 0.4% IPC gain vs prior MDP predictor

limitations: Not discussed; gains are measured on SPEC CPU 2017 and may not generalize to all memory-intensive workloads.
primary_theme: unified memory dependence and speculative bypass prediction
